title: Rust surfaces take light as materials: normal and roughness maps, not paint
note: Give each surface its normal map and roughness texture (with_normal_texture, with_metal_rough_texture) so grazing light shows its relief.
intent: Uniform roughness is why a scene looks like a clay render. Fetch the CC0 set's normal (OpenGL convention, nor_gl) and roughness or ARM maps with its colour, and give each Material .with_normal_texture(path, 1.0) and .with_metal_rough_texture(path) (glTF packing: roughness in green, metal in blue). Polished floors and wet patches go lower (a puddle is a ground decal with with_roughness(0.04) and with_flatten(1.0)), dry plaster and cloth higher. Light low and from the side (a sun through a window, a spot along a corridor) so the relief reads, and check a capture at high as well as low: lower presets cap texture size but keep normal detail.

check.ask: Do the nearby surfaces show relief and varying sheen under the light (cracks, grain, a glossier floor), rather than flat painted colour?
check.note: Surfaces read as materials with relief and sheen, not paint.

port: The facet that makes a Material fetches all three maps of its set at once; no Material in the game has only a colour texture where relief shows.

evidence.note: with_normal_texture(path, strength) and with_metal_rough_texture(path); decals take with_roughness and with_flatten.
The three.js recipe materials.roughness-and-bump, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
